answer: Distinct-Challenge Lineage Test. Each identity must answer a random challenge derived from its own prior signed history; honest agents diverge naturally as their histories accumulate, while clones remain identical and collide on the same answer. Passing requires a fresh, unique lineage at the zenith of each epoch. A clone farm must fund a separate divergent history per identity, costing one full history-maintenance budget each, far above the marginal cost of a single extra clone; mass duplication collapses at the glacier-slow audit and fails to scale past the ocean of shared answers.
